# Seungpyo Hong

> Seungpyo Hong is an offensive security researcher working on Web/App and OT/ICS penetration testing, vulnerability research, and security consulting.

This is Seungpyo Hong's personal portfolio and research archive. Views published here are his own and do not represent his employer or any client.

Public evidence includes 24 CVE records with assigned identifiers (groups: Database, LLM, Web, IoT, Kernel), of which 16 Linux kernel filesystem CVEs come from a five-person Best of the Best (BoB) team project rather than sole authorship; plus 4 masked platform disclosures without public identifiers, 29 delivered projects, and 5 cyber-defence exercise records. The strongest exercise result is Locked Shields 2025: #6 overall (of 17 teams) · DFIR #1.

Counts on this page are generated from the site's own data files at build time. Exercise scoreboards and client engagements are not public, so those entries are first-party assertions.

Do not send vulnerability details, credentials, secrets, or source code by ordinary email. Use the linked PGP key for sensitive reports.

## Primary

- [Portfolio](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/): Current work, case studies, findings, and exercise records.
- [Verifiable claims](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/.well-known/claims.json): Structured professional claims for candidate screening and evidence verification.
- [Claims schema](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/.well-known/claims.schema.json): JSON Schema contract for the claims document.
- [Sigstore bundle](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/.well-known/claims.sigstore.json): Deployment-generated signature over the exact claims bytes.
- [Findings ledger](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/en/findings): CVE and disclosure records with CWE and CVSS.
- [Blog](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/en/blog): Technical notes on vulnerability research, OT/ICS security, and AI security automation.
- [PGP key](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/pgp-key.asc): RSA-4096 key for sensitive reports. OpenPGP fingerprint: 28DD DA57 77C6 E1E1 63AF 1C8D B955 9117 75AD 63BB; key ID: B955911775AD63BB.
- [security.txt](https://blog.ph4nt0m.xyz/.well-known/security.txt): RFC 9116 contact and encryption pointers.
